reviews.text: This is E3.

A fun and fast-paced roguelike deckbuilder puzzle game. I'm used to games where I build up a deck of abilities that complement each other, but the additional factors of managing my puzzle board and finding abilities with overlapping inputs so I can try to activate several of them at once for as little mana as possible are new to me. I love it!

第四章需要+2难度或更高才能进入 平衡性有待调整，有的初始卡组甚至开局就暴毙，真的需要仔细打磨打磨。本身想法是很好的，但是实现的过程出现了一些偏差，比如本来石头三消放法术应该是很有运营的，结果小怪1-2回合结束，大怪和boss才会长那么一丢丢，那怎么放法术全看开局的随机石阵了、随机性让这个本来就很随机的游戏雪上加霜（我从未如此不喜欢随机性过）。而且有的角色初始卡组没回复，设计师你是希望我们靠第一关那个奶6去回复嘛？太幽默了，设计师你要不要自己玩玩看你设计的东西？这么喜欢设计无回复卡组，你咋不去设计一个没伤害的卡组呢？ 来自三个角色第一个牌组通关后：其实还是有优点的，玩起来比较爽，但是有的初始卡组是真的逆天，希望制作组好好考虑一下回复问题把。感觉游戏套不了端口化，需要一条路走到黑，尽可能拿能配合的法术和挂坠就会很轻松。imba的挂坠真的不少

On a fundamental level, the game is fun. However, the demo and the full version are different. The foes I encountered in the demo were fun to fight, while those in the full version are exhausting. They will constantly disable tiles on the field, summon cannon fodder, heal themselves and block. The constant disrupting and stalling is a frustrating experience.

之前試玩demo版本的第一章時 覺得不錯玩 就直接入手了 但正式版後覺得敵人難度有些增長太快 反觀我方角色能力強化覺得有點少 前期如果沒有穩定回血手段 幾乎很難撐過去 而後期則是需要有強力輸出或者彈幕攻擊 不然一次面對4隻小怪 真的很難打 希望商店增加能刷新的功能 增加玩家組出強力招式和徽章的機率 另外會希望打完小怪後 會有額外獎勵 例如打困難的小怪 能給一個隨機的徽章 或者提升幾點血量上限之類的獎勵 增加打怪的慾望和動力 因為很多原本普通的招式 再搭配一些適合的徽章的 就會變為很強的招式 所以如果能夠增加獲取徽章的機會 會增加可玩性 另外能不能增加一些提示 目前打過幾次第3章 只有一次進入到第4章 卻不知道是要符合什麼條件 才能解鎖第4章 還有成就中有幾隻敵人 也不知道要如何遇到 如果有誰知道 希望能提示一下 更新(發現開局選難度2以上好像就能進入第4章了 另外成就中的那幾隻敵人 在第4章好像就能刷到了) 這遊戲隱藏要素還真的不少 先是一次把商店的3招式和3徽章全買完 能額外解鎖一隻角色 另外隱藏更深的是在打到第4章後 畫面會出現10顆石頭的排列 之後在新一局的戰鬥當中 照著那10顆石頭的顏色順序打出來 就能開啟進入異界的新一層 (異界敵人難度不低 尤其關卡boss 真的超級難打 王會一直施展魔法護罩 你不照石頭順序去打 就會一直無敵 還會一直召喚會吸血的小兵 王還會一直強化攻擊力 真的是噁心到不行 難度極高 建議至少在招式組合完善後 再試著去挑戰) 在挑戰成功後 才會解鎖第5隻可操控角色 目前完成了不少隱藏任務 我就統一整理一下 方便大家攻略 首先有3隻隱藏角色的解鎖秘密任務 龐卡-一次買完商店的全部東西 即可解鎖 布洛德威(花妖)-完成儀式召喚花妖后 並打敗花妖 即可解鎖 冥后安隆-進入異界 打敗冥后安隆 即可解鎖 6隻腳色也分別有1個專屬的秘密任務 格溫-擊敗戰爭機甲 凱得麗溫-讓 召喚小妖 Imp 對蒼白蝰蛇造成致命一擊(這個我還沒完成 是看討論區有人表示有這個任務 ) 阿爾芬-擊敗帕魯格之貓 龐卡-購買商店中的所有物品 布洛德威-擊敗冥后安隆 冥后安隆-擊敗布洛德威 接下來是獎盃的秘密任務 黃獎盃 -分別使用6隻角色 通關第三幕(所以有6個獎盃) 紫獎盃- 分別使用6隻角色 通關第4幕 也就是至少用難度2以上去打 (也是有6個獎盃) 綠獎盃- 1.擊敗戰爭機角 2.進入異界 3.擊敗帕魯格之貓 4. 以難度4以上 完成一次遊戲 備註由於黃紫獎盃都有6個 所以我猜綠獎盃 應該還有2個秘密任務能解 但我目前也不知道 希望如果有人發現 能夠告知一下 感謝 補充-召換花妖方法 1.使用法術召喚儀式) 就是能使下一招咒語移除一個石頭 2.之後再選一個花費2石頭的法術 搭配上徽記(儀式匕首) 能減少咒語一個石頭的功能 3.讓法術變成0石頭花費 畫面就會出現亂碼的bug狀態 4.接著法術會出現隨機3石頭 就去完成 然後變隨機4石頭 完成 變隨機5石頭 再完成 5.花妖就會出現敵人位置 只要擊敗就能解鎖花妖 花妖就像第一幕的關底王的強化版本 也是不好打 戰爭機角-難度選擇出現下一幕的敵人後 在第4幕即可遇到 帕魯格之貓-一樣難度選擇出現下一幕敵人後 在異界能碰到
Legend of Bumbo if the dev wasn't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around 10/10
起初以为只能横竖连接 突然发现斜线也行 那就有点简单了 话说是不是有5个角色 最后两个角色怎么解锁呢 已经全部解锁了 游戏还在更新 给个好评吧
好玩小品 体量比较（相当）窄小 设计符合直觉交互流畅 确实有一种在施法的感觉 一次性拍出去好几个法术比较快乐 存在完爆的牌 开局资源的build基本就决定能不能活过第一层 属于是稍微琢磨一下就能感觉自己很聪明的那种游戏【大概

Without any consistent way of building defense or sustain, enemy encounters feel way too punishing and RNG-dependent. An unfavorable stone board can just mean eating 6 out of your 20 life before you really have an opportunity to do anything about it. Some characters mitigate this more than others, but this just doesn't feel as good as most examples of the genre.
一款结合连连看和爬塔的小游戏，上手难度不高，但是可玩性很高，玩着挺上头，希望能增加更多内容，让法术组合的选择更丰富

This game is an awesome twist on the typical deckbuilder experience, making the act of casting spells a simple puzzle that gets more complex as you try to unload your full spell list each turn. Until you craft a build around changing your gems to knives, in which case you stop worrying about puzzles and spells, and just start stabbin with a knife. 10/10 never bring a wizard to a knife fight

One of my favorite coffee break styled games of recent years. Simple, easy to understand mechanics with a lot of variety of possible builds and a charming art style. If you enjoy matching gems, this is a winner for sure!

The core gameplay of finding sequences of certain icons to cast the corresponding spells is a neat idea but in reality it isn't that fun and most of the RPG/roguelite elements are poorly implemented. A problem I didn't first expect when I started this game was the way the randomness of the core gameplay works out. In a typical deckbuilder, you have a large number of game pieces (often cards) which are randomly dealt to you each turn, but then playing them is pretty reliable. In this game, you have a smaller number of game pieces (spells) but whether or not you can play them at all is what is determined randomly by which stones appear on the board and where. It's very hard to feel like you're good at the sequence finding gameplay sections. It's usually very quickly obvious where the best path is so finding it is rarely hard and rarely satisfying (and sometimes there just isn't a good path to find). Instead, the entire game is more a test of how good you are at building a functional strategy out of what you get in shops and chests (and this too is pretty luck based). Some starting spell loadouts are terrible. On 2 occasions I've died in the first fight without anything I could do about it. I cast every spell possible to cast on each turn and still died. While it's impossible to tell after the first fight if any given death is my fault or not (ie did I make poor upgrade choices) it frequently feels like early game deaths are the result of poor luck rather than a lack of skill. The difficulty settings come from taking a variety of positive and negative modifiers before each run. However, the modifiers offered to you are random each time. This is annoying for two reasons. 1: You can't work to get good at working with or around certain predetermined modifiers. 2: Some positive modifiers are way stronger than others and some negative modifiers aren't nearly as dangerous as others, which leads to entire runs having massive variance in difficulty. If I'm to be totally fair to this game, I'll also share the 2 things I actually found interesting/fun about it. 1: The spell upgrade system can be fun. You can attach up to 2 badges to a spell to modify how it functions in a variety of ways (ie increasing damage, healing, changing the icon sequence to cast). Some spells benefit way more from some badges than others and finding the right combinations is pretty fun (ex. a badge that gives all numbers +1 works better on a spell that gives multiple buffs since it'll increase all of them). 2: An individual icon you highlight on the board can contribute to 2 spells simultaneously and the icons in a spell don't all have to be next to each other so long as they're in the right order. This means you can find spells with a lot of overlap in the casting sequence to cast them simultaneously at no extra cost (ex. If spell 1 has a sequence of Yellow, Red, Green and spell 2 has a sequence of just Yellow, Green, inputting a sequence of Yellow, Red, Green will cast both spells at once). This is an interesting kind of synergy that can only exist due to this game's unique resource system, and exploiting it is fun. I feel like if I can wring any enjoyment out of this game, it'll be while I'm playing on the lowest difficulty while watching something on my second monitor. The art is nice and getting some crazy build and blowing through enemies can be a fun time waster, but any time I try to engross myself in this game I just leave frustrated.

Oh my god this game is great. reminds me a lot of backpack hero, lots of options, cute art, and i'm already thinking up ways to break the game over my knee and make it sing for me. check this out if you can!
忒好玩了！可谓是相当上头，白天玩了晚上还想玩，半夜做梦都在想着搓暴风雪，然后爬起来接着玩。粘上了是饭不想吃，觉不想睡，上厕所都得一步三回头。神仙的艺术品，绝顶的好游戏，当榨菜就饭我能把盘子都吃下去。就写测评的这一小会我没玩着，现在都感觉身上刺挠。

[h1]能让人玩的不亦乐乎的精品小游戏[/h1] [hr][/hr] [h3]友情提示[/h3] 游戏用手柄体验会更加轻松哦，可以躺着玩的游戏 [h3]游戏体验[/h3] 游戏类型是类rogue加上消消乐，非常的有创意，是我今年玩过最有创意的独立游戏，非常吃头脑，策略性拉满，游戏主要玩法就是通过消消乐的连线来释放角色的技能，每个技能需要的消消乐方块的类型不一样，有红紫橙绿这几种方块，一开始的角色只有两个技能，但是这是个rogue游戏，你懂的，在探索的过程中，能通过购买或者是遇到法术地来选择想要的技能。这里的消消乐不是传统的消消乐，他是连线类型的消消乐，之前提到的技能释放需要按照顺序点亮一定数量和颜色的消消乐方块，但是游戏有法术的限制，也就是说不能无限释放，我们必须先想好我们的起点在哪里，终点在哪里，然后中途经过哪些方块。然后还有就是像贪吃蛇那样，不能从已经选定的方块中间穿过去，看技能能不能释放就看上面有没有光效就行。 [h3]游戏技巧[/h3] 有一个技巧就是你虽然需要按照那个顺序点亮，但是你中间可以是有其他不同颜色方块的，比如你需要蓝蓝方块来放一个盾的技能，这时候你连蓝橙蓝也可以达到同样的效果来释放你的盾的技能。活用这个技巧能让你在闯关的时候更加轻松，别以为到了一个死路上下左右没有一个需要的方块就无计可施了，这时候可以用跳跃思维，看看再往上下左右的地方有没有需要的方块，但是请注意你的魔力条，回合开始的时候为了限制玩家的强度，魔力条并不满，但随着探索，rogue的随机事件或者巧遇就能补充开始的魔力，也可以选择补充魔力上限； 还有一个技巧就是看清楚每个技能最前面和最后面需要什么方块，可以串起来，这样每个技能就可以少用一个方块和魔力； [h3]总结[/h3] 反正游戏挺有意思的，自己体验体验就可以感受到里面的魅力，非常推荐喜欢休闲小游戏的玩家购买，但是国区要68的价格我感觉略微有点小贵，如果能降到38-48这个价位即可无脑购入，吉米严选好游戏！ [quote]欢迎关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45531068/]黑白测评[/url] [hr]黑夜显真 白昼辨伪

[h1][b]宝石消除也肉鸽[/b][/h1] 《Witching Stone》将传统的宝石消除与Rogue玩法结合到了一起，用趣味的法术队列和可爱的像素风打造出了不错的游戏体验。 本作的基础玩法便是宝石消除，不过与三消类玩法不同，游戏中玩家可以用鼠标拖拽任意临近的宝石创造一条队列，被选中的宝石便会被消除。 作战中需要频繁用到的内容叫法术，其拥有各类不同的效果，如攻击、获得护盾、增加攻击力、创造新的宝石等。 这些法术上标注了对应的宝石，如初始角色的攻击便为红黄黄、护盾便为蓝蓝，只要玩家消除宝石的队列中包含这些前面的组合，便会释放对应法术。 这个设计非常巧妙，其直接舍弃了此类游戏的行动力系统，只要玩家操作得当，可以一回合内释放多个法术。 不过游戏仍然对其做了限制，一次性选择的宝石数量不能大于当前的法力值，而法力值则会在构筑中得到成长，这样一来很好的平衡了战斗。 游戏采用了《杀戮尖塔》那样的分支地图，玩家可在上面选择战斗、徽章、法术、商店、休息点等内容。 其中徽章是一系列增强法术的内容，如为法术附加强化攻击力、弱化敌人、回血等效果，玩家可按需搭配，此处尽量选择队列较少容易触发的法术，这样可以最大化收益。 游戏中敌人除了直接攻击玩家外，还会对棋盘做手脚，比如在其中增加无用的宝石、破坏宝石、为宝石增加负面效果等。 《Witching Stone》的这套玩法非常有新意，其将简单的休闲玩法扩展开来，使游戏的可玩性大幅提升，推荐喜欢策略类Rogue游戏的玩家一试。 [quote]关注鉴赏组：[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45134494]浮生评测[/url] ←"浮生若梦，一鉴倾心，邀您共赏人间烟火" 加入Steam组：[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/LLFLLFF]浮生评测[/url]←“一起追寻'浮生若梦'般的游戏体验” 开始“浮生若梦”鉴赏组的奇幻之旅！[/quote]

[h1] 非常有意思的解谜肉鸽游戏 [/h1] 《巫师石》是一款融合了消除与策略的2D类肉鸽游戏。 游戏的画风是个人比较喜欢的像素风格，我们的目标是变得强大，并击败关卡中的最后boss并进入下一关。 游戏的设计非常巧妙，因为你在游戏中的地图路径是固定的，在战斗方面点击遭遇战会进入战斗，有三个不同颜色的难度图标，分别对应简单，普通困难三个难度。 游戏中的战斗方式也非常的新颖，你只能在规定的5×4石头棋盘中绘制路径，石头必须相连，且不能超过你的法力值，法力值每回合后都会恢复。连接的方式可以上下左右，也可以斜着连接。释放法术的每块石头不需要是连续的，但顺序必须正确由左到右。连接好我们需要的石头后，点击执行就能释放攻击。 除了遭遇战，游戏中还有其他很多别的提升自己实力的方式，比如法术，徽记，营地，祝福，事件，商店这些，需要注意的是在商店中购买法术，需要消耗橡子，橡子的获取方式可以从遭遇战中获得。 在与敌人战斗中，我们可以从敌方角色上方看出本回合的意图，敌人的行动总是在我们之后的，这有助于我们规划战斗的方式。 徽记的特殊性可以给我们的法术增加亲的效果，但这也是一把双刃剑，我们需要进行合理的规划，才能使战斗变得轻松起来，有的徽记仅仅适用于固定的法术类型。 现阶段的游戏角色共有6个，初始角色格温，后续的角色需要完成游戏给予的目标才能解锁，在任务进度中，我们可以发现，随着游戏的进度增加，角色的初始法术也会有一个新的变化。 本作中可以解锁的东西很丰富，需要玩家自行在游戏中进行探索，游戏中还有着每日挑战这一系统，熟练了游戏机制的玩家不妨来尝试每日挑战，每次的挑战都给人一次全新的体验。 总的来说，游戏的战斗方式是非常新颖的，随机的地图路线与丰富的互动内容使人玩起来很上头，使用手柄体验效果更佳！ [quote] 亲亲亲！亲亲亲！噗铃噗铃！爱你爱你！姆尼姆尼！叻咯叻咯！姆拉姆拉！[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44515001]不动不动不动卿[/url]亲亲亲！亲亲亲！爱你爱你！姆尼姆尼！噗铃噗铃！波隆奴璐璐！叻咯叻咯！ [/quote]

Witching Stone, developed and published by Alexander Taylor, is an inventive blend of roguelite deckbuilding and spatial puzzle mechanics that delivers a fresh take on both genres. At its core, the game challenges players to cast spells by drawing paths through colored stones on a grid, with each combination activating a different effect based on your current build. What makes the game stand out is how it transforms what might seem like a basic match-based mechanic into a thoughtful, strategic system that rewards planning, experimentation, and adaptability. It’s a game that constantly pushes you to think several steps ahead while staying reactive to random elements that define roguelite gameplay. Players begin with a modest spellbook and a simple character, but as the run progresses, they accumulate new spells, enchantments, and passive bonuses that redefine their approach. The game isn’t just about stringing together the longest or most complex path — it's about finding synergy between your growing spell set and the dynamic board state. As new enemies appear with varied patterns, resistances, and disruptive abilities, you’re forced to adjust not only your pathing strategies but also your entire build philosophy. This system gives Witching Stone a satisfying learning curve, where each run brings new insights into optimal routes, spell synergy, and strategic risk-taking. The structure of the game is familiar to fans of roguelites. You traverse procedurally generated maps, choosing between battles, shops, rest points, events, and bosses. The tension lies in those decisions: do you push for a difficult elite fight for better rewards, or take a safer route and miss out on potential power spikes? These choices echo through each act, with long-term planning becoming essential for success. Boss battles punctuate each zone and serve as real skill checks — you can’t win by brute force alone; you must understand your tools and how to extract maximum value from your limited resources. Each failure feels like a lesson rather than a punishment, encouraging you to go back in with a revised strategy and greater knowledge. Visually, the game strikes a great balance between clarity and charm. The grid-based combat board is colorful but never cluttered, making it easy to track stone types and potential moves. Spell animations and effects are smooth, and each character has a unique design that adds personality without overwhelming the screen. Outside of battle, the UI is intuitive and responsive, with enough flavor in the menus and map designs to give the game a distinct identity. Music and sound design complement the pacing well — ambient tunes during exploration and more intense tracks during boss fights create an immersive and appropriately magical atmosphere. One of the game’s standout features is its character and modifier system. As you progress and complete objectives, you unlock new characters that dramatically shift your approach to combat. Each one comes with unique traits, opening up different strategies and spell interactions. Additionally, modifiers — which can be toggled before a run — add another layer of variety and challenge. Some increase enemy health, others limit your spell pool, or add environmental hazards that alter the grid. These elements greatly enhance replayability, allowing players to customize their experience and test their mastery in increasingly demanding scenarios. However, the game does have a few areas where it might not satisfy every kind of player. Because of its puzzle-centric core, turns can take a while — especially in the late game where builds become more complex and the cost of a misstep is higher. For those who prefer fast-paced or reactive gameplay, this methodical pace may feel like a slowdown. There’s also a learning curve tied to understanding how spells interact, and while the game tries to be intuitive, some effects and modifiers aren’t always clearly explained, which could be frustrating in high-stakes situations. The occasional opacity in mechanics might put off players who value complete transparency in combat systems. Despite these minor drawbacks, Witching Stone is a remarkable achievement, especially considering its indie origins. It successfully merges the addictive experimentation of deckbuilders with the cerebral satisfaction of puzzle-solving, creating a hybrid that feels fresh and thoughtfully crafted. The progression feels rewarding without being grindy, and every run carries the potential for both surprising victories and humbling defeats. Most importantly, it’s a game that respects the player’s intelligence — it challenges without hand-holding, but never feels unfair or deliberately obtuse. In the end, Witching Stone stands as a polished, creative, and deeply satisfying entry in the roguelite genre. It’s ideal for players who enjoy careful planning, theorycrafting, and adapting to ever-changing circumstances. While its deliberate pace and depth may not suit everyone, those who give it the time and attention it asks for will find it rich with strategic potential and long-term enjoyment. It’s not just a game about drawing lines on a board — it’s about forging a path through chaos, one stone at a time. Rating: 8/10

Hate not to like it, but it just misses the mark for the genre. Builds and developing them feels extremely sluggish, characters are vastly different from the start, up to the point where the second character is borderline unplayable if you don't get lucky on the first map since she starts with 0 defensive moves. Altogether, it seems extremely underbaked and I hate to say that, because the game certainly does have its charms and you can do interesting things with some of the badges, which essentially modify your spells. But again, some are like absolutely no brainers to take if you get them and others feel like they provide you with a minor advantage for massive drawbacks. I see the honest attempt to make something a bit different, which is commendable in the times of "formula X for the win", I don't see, however, the actual attempt to make the game good. Not sure if that comes from a lack of experience or unwillingness, but the base mechanics are solid and it should not be hard to go from there, but the top layer, which is where player agency is involved, feels like a bad attempt of a minimalistic card battler. Add to that, that this game is much RNG heavier than an actual card battler, it never feels good if you die because you get a rotten board right at the final boss when you most need it, while you went 95% of the game with that setup. Combined with extremely lazy boss/enemy mechanics (only boss with random second phase, while also the only boss that has a "max dmg/turn" shield in both phases), it feels consistently like the devs have no idea how to balance things or how to make the game interesting. Some enemies just literally get invul buffs that you need 2-3 turns to realistically clear off and that's just stupid and furthers the impression nobody actually tested the game. And to round it off, some things are just incredibly broken or unclear and either do not work as described or there seems to be a language barrier. In either case, not great for a 10$ game at this point. For that price, I at least expect that certain things are being correctly tracked in the game. "Beat the game with 2 characters to unlock (progress 0/2)", although I beat the game with a character.... stuff like that. It's like playing DnD with a stubborn 13 year old as a DM, that realised your character smokes everything in 95% of all cases, so they specifically craft a final boss that hard counters everything you do with zero chance of preparation or adaption on your side. That's the biggest gripe, once you are in battle, all things are set in stone, just luck involved. No way to adapt to new challenges or abilities. Doesn't feel good, because you essentially play a long fight for no other reason to lose, since you know you're done because the boss and the character's abilities are hard counters. There is a way to "view" the boss beforehand, but it doesn't tell you what they can actually do. So what's the point here? Altogether, it is a cute game, it certainly has a bit of novelty to it, but altogether, I fail to see any real attempt to fix the multiple issues this game has with balance, adaptability, overrealiance on RNG and very particular mechanics, boss design and character design. Hate not to love it, here's to hoping the devs work on it in the future, which is when I gladly will give it another spin. That being said: There is a demo, just don't think that there is more to it than there is in the demo. That's it, really. Sure, there are more levels, but they literally play the same. But if you like the demo, chances are good you enjoy this too. Would love to give it a ~, but steam forces me to give a thumbs down, at least for now. Positively, I cannot stress enough the eye for detail. Your spellbook is in the lower left corner and you immediately see defensive and offensive spells as they are denoted in different colours, even in the icon, without needing to open the book. It's details like that that make me hope these devs really do more and just get some experience in the market and genres they like to do, because, damn, there is potential here. A lot of cryptic stuff, badly worded items which is not clear how they work, e.g. "era" So please, do not think of me being harsh for no reason. You're doing good. Keep at it! Edit for the dev: Thanks for proving my point while focusing on some throwaway phrases that clearly go over your head while missing the essential part entirely. This is a fresh take on the roguelite genre. Instead of a deck, you have a spellbook. You start with 2 spells and can go up to 6. They all start as available - no shuffling and drawing cards required. There is a gem grid that corresponds to the costs required to cast the spells. Connect the gems in the right sequences, and you cast the spell. The tutorial is pretty good, although there are a lot of mechanics at play, and it's sometimes difficult to figure out what is going to happen. The tooltips are quite good, but still sometimes it's hard to understand who (you or your opponent) will be affected by a spell. As you learn the mechanics on both sides, the gameplay becomes smoother. The spells light up when you're going to cast them, and the gem sequences also appear below your character. The placement is weird because you're staring at your spellbook, not looking below your character, so it's not easily noticed. Might be better placed somewhere inside the spellbook. As you click on the gems, it "highlights" the path, but the colors are sometimes difficult to differentiate from the regular board (the unselected gems). You can undo your selection one gem at a time with the right mouse button, which is very helpful. There are 6 characters. The first one is probably the easiest to play. The next two are easy to unlock. The next one is a bit more difficult to unlock. The last two are crazy difficult to unlock! I could see why some players would stop after 3 or 4 characters. I like that they all have different play styles and dialogue. I'm unsure if they have "class spells" (spells specific to the character), but I suspect they do, and that adds a nice bit of variety as well. There's a lot of content here! You'll be hooked for a while. There are also badges, which "upgrade" your spells. They're pretty good, but you can only equip a certain number (default 2) to each spell. You can unlock modifiers, which let you make the game easier or harder. You need to play the harder modifiers (think ascension mode) if you want the full experience (no spoilers here). I like that there are in-game "quests", which are mostly different from the Steam achievements, although there is some overlap. It lets you unlock new badges and starting decks for the characters. I think this is a great meta-game mechanic. As for balance, I found some of the characters very difficult to play. You need to have a good mix of attack and defense spells. Sometimes, there are no defensive spells that give you block or heal you, and then you just lose. I'm not sure if that's related to the character, or just RNG. Ok, I will try again! But it's not a great feeling. There are also some spells that I think, "Why would I ever use this?". Maybe I'm just missing something. There are some modifiers that are like, "How would this ever be fun?". Overall, the starting / act 1 spells are rather weak, and they get better the farther into the run you go, so in that regard, it is well balanced. I like the maps being open such that you can go back to nodes after exploring further (but not once you proceed to the next act/map). For example, you might be given a choice of spell, but there's also a shop coming up and want to explore that first - you can! You can also save rest sites for when you need them, which is awesome. I like the blessings - all good choices which make a big impact on your gameplay. The core gameplay loop is solid. Aside from sometimes being very confused about what happened (no history tiles), the game is great and pretty addictive. I think the design is spot on, even if some of the characters are more frustrating than others. Overall excellent, and would definitely recommend!
